Opt. Soc. Am. 64, 891 (1974), which could not be opened (publisher access only); no laser measurement located

Branching fractions / A values of the 4p2 5s - 4p3 lines newer than NIST: Berzins, Ubelis, Bziskjans, J. Quant. Spectrosc. Radiat. Transfer 276, 107943 (2021) (26 lines, 7 upper levels) and Lotrian, Guern, Cariou, J. Phys. B 13, 685 (1980) exist but only their abstracts could be read (publisher bot walls); no table values entered

Hyperfine constants of 75As in excited levels of 4p2 5s, 4s4p4, 4p2 4d (Bouazza et al., Z. Phys. D 7, 33 and 185 (1987); Voss, Weiss, Winkler, Physica B+C 123, 121 (1983)): papers not accessible; only the 4p3 metastable A constants quoted by Liu et al. 2023 are entered, without B

Measured Lande g factors (Li and Andrew, J. Opt. Soc. Am. 70, 719 (1980), 61 g values; Green and Barrows 1935): paper not accessible; only the ground-level g_J from Pendlebury and Smith is entered. Calculated g_J of the 4p3 levels exist in Liu et al. 2023 Table VII but were left out because measurements exist
Measured lifetimes / A values of the metastable 4p3 2D, 2P levels: no measurement located; theory (Liu et al. 2023 MRCI, Garstang 1964) given instead
Isotope shifts: 75As is the only stable isotope, none applicable. Precise (laser) transition frequencies: none located
Ionization energy: nothing more precise than the NIST value 78950(2) cm^-1 located
The web-search tool was unavailable in this session (search budget exhausted), so sources were located only by following NIST bibliography entries, DOIs and reference lists
conflicts: 5s 4P lifetimes: laser 4.5(5) ns (4P1/2) and 4.3(5) ns (4P3/2) (Bengtsson et al. 1992) vs beam-foil 3.6(4) and 3.8(4) ns (Andersen et al. 1974); laser values kept

Resonance-line f values: Bengtsson et al. 1992 print f(193.7 nm) = 0.123(17) and f(197.2 nm) = 0.059(8); the abstract of Berzins et al. 2021 prints '197.3 nm, f = 0.127, and 193.8 nm f = 0.059', i.e. the same two numbers attached to the opposite lines. Full text of Berzins et al. not accessible, so this was not resolved; Bengtsson's assignment agrees with NIST ASD (A = 2.19e8 and 2.02e8 s^-1)
NIST Handbook of Basic Atomic Spectroscopic Data (older) lists A = 2.2e8 (193.76 nm), 2.0e8 (197.26 nm) and 2.7e8 s^-1 (189.04 nm), from Morton 2000; consistent with the values here

Metastable lifetimes (theory only): MRCI 21(3), 248(4), 1.08(2), 0.47(1) s (Liu et al. 2023) vs 12-13, 143-177, 0.77-0.85, 0.34-0.55 s (Garstang 1964; Biemont and Hansen 1986); the forbidden-line A values entered under transitions are Garstang's and therefore correspond to the shorter lifetimes
notes: Level energies are the NIST ASD values (data/nist/As_I_levels.tsv). 75As has I = 3/2 and is the only stable isotope. The two resonance-line A values are derived from the absorption oscillator strengths printed by Bengtsson et al. (their laser lifetimes combined with the branching ratios of Lotrian et al. 1980); NIST ASD already lists the same numbers. Hyperfine A constants of the 4p3 2D, 2P levels are second-hand (Bouazza et al. 1987 as quoted by Liu et al. 2023); note the large uncertainty of 2P°3/2. Lifetimes of the 4p3 metastable levels and all forbidden-line rates are THEORY. In the forbidden-line entries A_s is the sum of the calculated M1 and E2 rates and the note gives both parts.
